Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent.relations

Class MorphMap

java.lang.Object
org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent.relations.MorphMap
public final class MorphMap extends Object
The global map between morph aliases and model classes, a port of Laravel's Relation::morphMap, enforceMorphMap and requireMorphMap.

A polymorphic relation stores a type string beside the id. With a map, the string is an alias such as posts; without one it is the class name. The map is a strict two-way map: one alias per class and one class per alias, so getMorphAlias(Class) is never ambiguous. Aliases compare as exact strings, so "0" is a valid alias. A null or empty alias is refused.

The map is required by default: a class with no alias fails with ClassMorphViolationException instead of writing its class name. requireMorphMap(boolean) with false lets a class without an alias use its class name. In that mode a stored class name is loaded through the model's class loader without initialising it, and refused unless the class is a Model. This is the library's only reflective class lookup.

The state is one immutable snapshot behind a volatile field. Reads take one volatile read and see a consistent map; writes are synchronised and replace the snapshot. The map is shared by every database manager in the JVM.

The map holds strong Class references and cannot unregister an entry. In a redeploying container the old class loader stays pinned, and registering a reloaded class under the same alias is refused because the alias is still bound to the old class. A map per database manager is planned.

  • Method Details

    • morphMap

      public static void morphMap(Map<String,Class<? extends Model>> map)
      Adds aliases to the map; an alias already bound to the same class is left alone.

      The call is all or nothing: when one entry is refused, none is added.

      Parameters:
      map - the aliases and their classes, never null, with no null key, empty key or null class
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if map, a class or an alias is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if an alias is empty, an alias is already bound to another class, or a class is already under another alias
